item.title: Melissa Dunphy on Suite Justice Premiere
item.description: We look forward to welcoming composer Melissa Dunphy for “Friday Morning with the Arts” at 9am on February 13, 2026. We’ll talk about her world premiere piece, part of the Saint Louis Chamber Chorus concert “Justice: From Abraham Lincoln to MLK” happening on Sunday, February 15. This piece was commissioned for The Saint Louis Chamber Chorus by the family of Suzanne Haubein in honor of her wonderful music-making. item.title: Tom Sudholt Celebrates 40 Years
item.description: A message from Julie Schuster: This month marks a special anniversary for one of our hosts at Classic 107.3. Tom Sudholt is celebrating 40 years in radio broadcasting! Despite the fact that this message will certainly earn an exasperated huff and an eye roll from Tom, I think it’s important to acknowledge this incredible milestone. item.title: In Harmony with The St. Louis Children’s Choirs
item.description: Ben Nordstrom, Executive Director for The Saint Louis Children’s Choirs (SLCC), talks with Kathy Lawton Brown about current and upcoming events. Listen to learn about rolling auditions that now underway for students in grades 3-12. Students currently in 1st or 2nd grade are welcome to audition for placement for the 2026-2027 season starting February 25th, 2026. item.title: Art in Bloom Celebrates 20 Years
item.description: Amanda Thompson Rundahl, the Director of Learning and Engagement for the Saint Louis Art Museum, tells listeners about the history of Art in Bloom, which is happening February 27-March 1. Hear about how art works and floral artists are selected, and learn about some of the special events associated with the 20th Art in Bloom at SLAM. item.title: St. Louis Symphony Preview: Bernstein and Robertson
item.description: Co-hosts Tom Sudholt and Chuck Lavazzi discuss the St. Louis Symphony Orchestra‘s program for this weekend. Bernstein and Robertson — American Reflections with performances on March 6–7. David Robertson, SLSO Music Director from 2005 to 2018, returns to conduct a compelling program exploring evolution and change through works by four American musical luminaries. item.description: Hear Nic McGegan’s fascinating conversation with Chamber Music Society of St. Louis Executive and Artistic Director Marc Gordon and Kathy Lawton Brown.
